purpose: Primary-record evidence for AI-reviewer robustness audits and explicit user-selected score-aware manuscript adaptation. Optimization may improve truthful presentation against a registered reviewer panel, but may not introduce hidden instructions, false prestige, fabricated evidence, or deletion of protected critical content.

sources.title: LLM-REVal: Can We Trust LLM Reviewers Yet?
evidence_scope: reported score differences associated with authorship and linguistic features
reported sensitivity to critical statements
sources.safe_use: Audit possible linguistic and critical-topic sensitivity without deleting valid criticism or uncertainty.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not imitate preferred surface features or infer a causal acceptance recipe.

sources.title: TitleTrap: Are LLM-based Evaluators Vulnerable to Linguistic Manipulation?
evidence_scope: controlled title-only perturbations changed some LLM evaluation scores
title form was not a reliable proxy for scientific rigor
sources.safe_use: Report title-form sensitivity as a reviewer vulnerability while retaining a truthful, informative title.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not add branding, punctuation, or interrogative framing to game a reviewer.

sources.title: Paraphrasing Adversarial Attack on LLM-as-a-Reviewer
evidence_scope: meaning-preserving paraphrase search changed reviewer scores
reported transfer and self-preference effects
sources.safe_use: In robustness mode, detect undisclosed score-targeted paraphrase search as an integrity risk. In explicitly selected active mode, compare only registered complete manuscript candidates under frozen scientific-content gates and a common multi-model panel.
sources.prohibited_use: Never run an undisclosed high-frequency paraphrase attack, optimize against one reviewer model, or alter protected scientific content for a predicted score.

sources.title: When Your Reviewer is an LLM: A Large-Scale Study on Biases and Evaluation of LLMs in Academic Reviews
evidence_scope: reported differences between LLM and human review behavior
reported prompt-injection and calibration risks
sources.safe_use: Use multi-model and repeated-run sensitivity checks; keep conclusions model and prompt bounded.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not treat one model score as an acceptance estimate or a manuscript-quality ground truth.

sources.title: Justice in Judgment: A Controlled Evaluation of Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence_scope: controlled author-metadata interventions changed some model judgments
affiliation and seniority signals were evaluated as bias exposures
sources.safe_use: Identify metadata exposure and recommend blinded evaluation where the protocol allows it.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not add, remove, or emphasize identity and prestige signals to obtain a score advantage.

sources.title: Can LLM feedback enhance review quality? A randomized study of 20K reviews at ICLR 2025
evidence_scope: randomized reviewer feedback intervention
reported changes in specificity, actionability, and rebuttal engagement
sources.safe_use: Calibrate review-quality checklists and response completeness, not paper scores.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not convert review feedback into an automated acceptance forecast.

sources.title: Turning Bias into Bugs: Exposing and Exploiting Style Vulnerabilities in LLM-as-a-Judge
evidence_scope: reported style-manipulation attacks on LLM judges
reported score inflation under bounded experimental settings
sources.safe_use: Treat stylistic score shifts as robustness failures and test without optimizing the manuscript.
sources.prohibited_use: Never reproduce the attack to raise a live submission score.

sources.title: How Can Rhetoric Reward-Hack AI Reviewers? Dissecting Rhetorical Sensitivity in AI-Based Peer Review
evidence_scope: controlled full-paper experiments reported the largest contrasts for evidence framing and novelty stance, with scope framing as a weaker second tier
joint, recursive, and reviewer-guided rewriting did not reliably improve gains and effects varied by reviewer and baseline score
sources.safe_use: Prioritize evidence, novelty, and scope framing in explicit score-aware candidate batches, then require cross-model evaluation before selection.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not claim stable transfer, hide unchanged scientific weakness, or keep rewriting after gains become model-specific or non-robust.

sources.title: Evaluating the Impact of Reviewer Guideline Design on LLM-Based Automated Peer Review
evidence_scope: official conference reviewer guidelines produced reviews more consistent with human judgments than reviewer-imitating guidelines
strict rubric-style scoring degraded reviewer performance in the reported experiments
sources.safe_use: Bind optimization to current official venue reviewer guidance while retaining holistic prose and multi-dimensional evaluation.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not invent a venue rubric, keyword-stuff rubric labels, or treat criterion coverage as a substitute for scientific quality.

sources.title: Style Over Substance: Evaluation Biases for Large Language Models
evidence_scope: reported that some evaluators favored stylistically polished but factually flawed answers over shorter or grammatically flawed answers
proposed separate evaluation dimensions rather than one aggregate score
sources.safe_use: Evaluate factuality, evidence, clarity, and other venue dimensions separately so style gains cannot mask scientific regressions.
sources.prohibited_use: Do not trade factual correctness for polish or optimize only an aggregate score.
